papers.title: Mechanical Properties and Fracture Behavior of Hot Isostatically Pressed TiC/TC4 Composites
papers.abstract: Titanium matrix composites (TMCs), characterized by low density, high strength, and excellent high-temperature mechanical properties, are becoming preferred materials for key components in aerospace engines. However, conventional casting methods for preparing TMCs often encounter issues such as composition segregation and coarse reinforcement phases, hindering their engineering application. In this study, we fabricated TiC/TC4 titanium matrix composites via hot isostatic pressing (HIP). The composites exhibited room-temperature tensile strength of 1058 ± 8 MPa, yield strength of 958 ± 12 MPa, and total elongation of 17.0 ± 0.5%. Furthermore, the TiC/TC4 composites demonstrated favorable high-temperature mechanical properties, with a tensile strength of about 500 MPa at 600 °C. Investigation into plastic deformation and fracture behavior revealed that at room temperature, tensile cracks initiated predominantly around the reinforcing TiC particles, whereas at high temperatures, cracks primarily originated within the matrix. The strengthening mechanisms of the TiC particle-reinforced TC4 composites included particle strengthening, solid solution strengthening, and load-transfer strengthening. Additionally, the precipitation of nano-acicular secondary α (αs) phases within the β phase during high-temperature tensile deformation was observed, contributing to the superior high-temperature mechanical performance of the composites.

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文涉及热等静压处理TC4基复合材料，但未涉及增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的后处理对疲劳性能的影响。
llm.why_not_core: The paper studies HIP-fabricated TiC/TC4 composites, not post-processing of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V, and does not report fatigue data.

summary_en.motivation: To overcome composition segregation and coarse reinforcement phases in conventionally cast titanium matrix composites.
summary_en.method: TiC/TC4 composites were fabricated via hot isostatic pressing and characterized for tensile and fracture behavior.
summary_en.result: The composites achieved room-temperature tensile strength of 1058 MPa, yield strength of 958 MPa, and total elongation of 17%, with high-temperature strength of ~500 MPa at 600°C.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing including room-temperature and high-temperature tensile tests was performed.

papers.title: A novel small punch creep test to determine norton creep properties of LPBF Ti64 alloy
papers.abstract: Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) Ti-6Al-4V (Ti64)alloy is increasingly favored in additive manufacturing (AM) for complex, lightweight, and high-strength components. However, the inherent microstructural heterogeneity in LPBF materials necessitates specialized characterization methods to ensure reliable performance in service conditions. The Small Punch Creep Test (SPCT) has gained recognition as an innovative and efficient technique for assessing materials creep behavior, particularly beneficial for AM components allowing easier sampling and local characterization of microstructure heterogeneities. Although standards such as CWA 15627 and EN 10371 provide empirical correlations between SPCT and uniaxial creep test (UCT) results, the complex deformation mechanisms in LPBF materials, including anisotropy, porosity, and phase evolution, necessitate material-specific calibration for accurate interpretation. This study proposes a direct methodology to derive the Norton creep parameters of LPBF Ti64 alloy from both Small Punch Test (SPT) and SPCT data, integrating a new representative stress-strain method with inverse finite element analysis (FEA). By first extracting elasto-plastic properties from SPT using the representative stress-strain method, the model enables efficient extraction of Norton creep parameters through inverse analysis of SPCT results. Experimental validation on LPBF Ti64 alloy demonstrates strong agreement with properties derived from SPCT, verifying the accuracy and practical applicability of the proposed method for AM components.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文针对LPBF Ti64合金的蠕变性能测试方法，虽然不直接涉及疲劳，但属于力学性能表征，与研究方向相关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on creep properties, which are not explicitly listed in the direction's focus on tensile, fatigue, and hardness; it does not provide direct fatigue or tensile data.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发适用于LPBF Ti64合金的小冲杆蠕变测试方法以获取Norton蠕变参数。
summary_zh.method: 结合代表应力-应变法和逆有限元分析，从小冲杆测试和蠕变测试中提取参数。
summary_zh.result: 实验验证表明该方法与理论一致，准确性高。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a novel small punch creep test method for LPBF Ti64 alloy to determine Norton creep parameters efficiently.
summary_en.method: A combined representative stress-strain method and inverse finite element analysis is used to extract creep parameters from small punch test data.
summary_en.result: The method shows strong agreement with uniaxial creep test results, confirming its accuracy.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through small punch creep tests and comparison with uniaxial creep tests.

papers.title: A Dynamic Time Warping-Transfer Learning Approach to Transferring Knowledge in Stress-strain Behaviors from Polymers to Metals: An Affordable and Generalizable Additive Manufacturing Part Qualification Framework
papers.abstract: Part qualification in additive manufacturing (AM) ensures that additively manufactured parts can be consistently produced and reliably used in critical applications. One crucial aspect of part qualification is to determine the complex stress-strain behavior of additively manufactured parts. However, conventional part qualification techniques such as the destructive testing and non-destructive testing are costly and time consuming, especially for metal AM. To address this challenge, we develop a dynamic time warping (DTW)-transfer learning (TL) framework for AM part qualification by transferring knowledge gained from the stress-strain behaviors of additively manufactured low-cost polymers to high-performance, expensive metals. Specifically, the framework selects one single optimal polymer dataset that is the most similar to the metal dataset in the target domain using DTW among multiple polymer datasets, including Nylon, PLA, CF-ABS, and Resin. A long short-term memory (LSTM) model is then trained on one single optimal polymer dataset and tested on one of three target metal datasets, including AlSi10Mg, Ti6Al4V, and carbon steel datasets. Experimental results show that the Resin dataset is selected as the optimal polymer dataset in the source domain for the AlSi10Mg and Ti6Al4V datasets, while the Nylon dataset is selected as the optimal polymer dataset in the source domain for the carbon steel dataset. The DTWTL model trained on one single optimal polymer dataset as the source domain achieves the best predictive performance, including an average mean absolute percentage error of 12.41%, an average root mean squared error of 63.75, and an average coefficient of determination of 0.96 when three metals are used as the target domain, outperforming the vanilla LSTM model without TL as well as the TL model trained on all four polymer datasets as the source domain.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要关注一种通用的迁移学习方法，将聚合物应力应变知识转移到金属材料，Ti6Al4V仅作为其中一个测试案例，不专注于Ti6Al4V的力学或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: Paper does not focus on Ti-6Al-4V mechanical/fatigue characterization; it uses Ti-6Al-4V as one of three test datasets for a general ML framework transferring knowledge from polymers to metals.

summary_zh.motivation: 提出一种低成本增材制造部件鉴定方法，通过迁移聚合物知识预测金属应力应变。
summary_zh.method: 利用动态时间规整选择最优聚合物数据集，训练LSTM模型预测金属应力应变曲线。
summary_zh.result: 在AlSi10Mg、Ti6Al4V和碳钢上取得良好预测精度（MAPE 12.41%）。
summary_zh.validation: 基于文献中的公开实验数据集进行数值验证。

summary_en.motivation: Develop a cost-effective part qualification framework for metal additive manufacturing by transferring knowledge from polymer stress-strain behaviors.
summary_en.method: Use dynamic time warping to select the optimal polymer dataset and train an LSTM model to predict metal stress-strain curves.
summary_en.result: The DTW-TL model achieves high prediction accuracy on AlSi10Mg, Ti6Al4V, and carbon steel datasets with an average MAPE of 12.41%.
summary_en.validation: Validated on existing experimental stress-strain datasets from the literature.
